oNas.uvod: Šeherezada is a family-run place that has been serving halal kebab and fast food in Ljubljana since 1998. We started with a single vertical grill on Trubarjeva; today you will find us at two addresses, with a third on the way.
oNas.pocetak.p1: The first location was a small space on Trubarjeva with room for two people behind the counter and nobody else. The marinade recipe came from our grandfather in Istanbul and he never wrote it down — the grandchildren learned it by watching.
oNas.pocetak.p2: For the first few years we made only kebab. Pizzas arrived in 2006, when we put a stone oven in the space next door, and burgers only ten years later, when guests started asking for them often.
oNas.razlika.p1: We carve the meat by hand, not with a machine. It takes longer and needs a person at the grill the whole time, but the slices are thicker and stay juicy. We bake the bread every morning and distribute it, so it is never from yesterday.
oNas.razlika.p2: We stay open longer than most. At weekends the Trubarjeva location runs until five in the morning, because we believe good food should be available when most kitchens have long closed.
oNas.ekipa.p1: There are eleven people behind the counter, five of whom have been with us for more than ten years. The chef who runs the meat preparation started as a student on a summer job and stayed fifteen years.
oNas.halal.p1: All meat is halal without exception, and we prepare it separately from everything else. There is no pork in the kitchen and we use no alcohol. We write in more detail about the sourcing and handling on its own page.
halal.uvod: All our meat is halal, and that applies to every dish on the menu — not just the kebab, but the burgers and pizzas too. This page explains what that means in practice: where the meat comes from, how we handle it, and why there is no alcohol in the kitchen.
halal.pomen.p1: Halal means food prepared according to the rules set out in Islamic law. For meat this concerns the method of slaughter and how the animal is treated beforehand; for everything else it means the absence of forbidden ingredients — above all pork and alcohol.
halal.meso.p1: We source beef and veal from two suppliers in Slovenia and Austria, both holding a valid halal certificate. Chicken comes from a third. We verify the certificates once a year and whenever we change supplier.
halal.certifikat.p1: The certificate hangs on the wall beside the till in every location, so you can read it before ordering. If you would like a copy, the staff will send one by e-mail.
halal.odvojeno.p1: Since there is no pork in the kitchen at all, cross-contact is not possible. The meat has its own work surface, its own boards and its own knives, used for nothing else. Vegetarian dishes also have their own preparation area.
halal.bezAlkohola.p1: We use no alcohol anywhere — not in sauces, not in dough, not in marinades. Even the vinegar is an alcohol-free substitute. We do not serve alcoholic drinks and they are not on the menu.
galerija.uvod: Photographs of the food, the spaces and the people behind the counter. The pictures were taken in both locations, most of them early in the morning or late at night when it is quietest.
faq.uvod: We have collected the twenty-four questions guests ask most often — about halal and ingredients, about opening hours and locations, and about ordering and prices. If you cannot find your answer, give us a call.

zasebnost.zbiramo.p1: The website requires no registration and collects no personal data. If you call us or order through delivery, we process only the data needed to fulfil the order.
zasebnost.piskotki.p1: We use only technical cookies that remember your chosen theme and language. We use no tracking cookies and no advertising tools.

pogoji.cene.p1: Prices on the website include tax and apply to the location named at the top of the menu. Prices differ between locations. We reserve the right to change prices without prior notice.
pogoji.dostava.p1: Delivery runs through Wolt and Glovo, which are independent providers. Their terms govern delivery times and the state of the order. We also accept complaints about food quality directly.
pogoji.reklamacije.p1: If something is wrong with your order, call the location where you ordered. If the mistake is ours, we replace the dish at no extra cost.

faqH.meso.pitanje: Is all the meat really halal?
faqH.meso.odgovor: Yes, all our meat is halal. We source it from certified suppliers whose certification we verify once a year. This applies to all three locations and every dish on the menu — burgers and pizzas included, not just the kebab.
faqH.svinjina.pitanje: Is there pork in your kitchen?
faqH.svinjina.odgovor: No, there is no pork in our kitchen at all. We do not use it in any dish, sauce or filling. Since it is not on the premises, cross-contact during preparation is not possible.
faqH.alkohol.pitanje: Do you use alcohol in cooking?
faqH.alkohol.odgovor: We do not use it anywhere. Not in the sauces, not in the pizza dough, not in the marinades. Even the vinegar we use is an alcohol-free substitute. We do not serve alcoholic drinks.
faqH.certifikat.pitanje: Where can I see the certificate?
faqH.certifikat.odgovor: The certificate hangs on the wall next to the till in every location. If you want a closer look, the staff will gladly show it. We can also send a copy by e-mail.
faqH.vegetarijansko.odgovor: We do. Falafel in yufka and the falafel plate are fully plant-based, as are the fries and the seasonal salad. Among the pizzas, margherita and vegetariana are vegetarian. Every dish on the menu is labelled if it is vegetarian or vegan.
faqH.alergeni.pitanje: Where do I find the allergens?
faqH.alergeni.odgovor: With every dish on the menu — click on it and a list of ingredients and allergens opens. If you have a severe allergy, tell us when ordering so we can prepare the dish separately.
faqH.kruh.odgovor: Yes, we bake the bread and flatbreads every day at the Trubarjeva location and distribute them in the morning. The pizza dough proofs for twenty-four hours, which gives it a thinner crust and better flavour.
faqH.pikantno.odgovor: Most dishes are not spicy. Those that are carry a chilli marker on the menu — one means mild, three means very hot. You can always order the spicy sauce on the side or leave it out.
faqC.najdlje.pitanje: Which location is open the longest?
faqC.najdlje.odgovor: Trubarjeva. On Fridays and Saturdays it is open until five in the morning, and until two on weekdays. The Slovenska location closes at midnight, so for a late meal we recommend Trubarjeva.
faqC.prazniki.pitanje: Are you open on public holidays?
faqC.prazniki.odgovor: Mostly yes, but with different hours. We are closed on Christmas Day, we close at six in the evening on New Year's Eve, and open only at noon on New Year's Day. Exceptions are posted on the location page.
faqC.sedezi.odgovor: The Slovenska location has twenty seats and tables by the window, suitable for a proper sit-down lunch. Trubarjeva is smaller and mainly for takeaway, though it has some standing room.
faqC.parking.odgovor: Trubarjeva is in a pedestrian zone; the nearest garage is Kongresni trg, a five-minute walk. Near Slovenska there is blue-zone street parking, and in the evenings it is often free.
faqC.dostopnost.odgovor: The Slovenska location is entirely at street level and has no threshold. Trubarjeva has one low step at the entrance; the staff will gladly help if you call ahead.
faqN.kako.odgovor: The fastest way is by phone or straight at the counter. For delivery use Wolt or Glovo. We do not take orders through the website for now, because we want the food to be fresh when you arrive.
faqN.dostava.odgovor: No, delivery runs through Wolt and Glovo. Their couriers cover central Ljubljana and the surrounding area. Delivery usually takes between twenty and forty-five minutes.
faqN.kartice.odgovor: We accept all common cards as well as phone payments. Cash is of course equally welcome. For amounts under five euros the card works with no surcharge.
faqN.boni.pitanje: Do you accept student meal vouchers?
faqN.boni.odgovor: Yes, in both open locations. The student menu includes a main course of your choice, soup, salad, an apple and a drink. Any surcharge depends on the main course chosen and is stated on the menu.
faqN.cene.pitanje: Why do prices differ between locations?
faqN.cene.odgovor: Because rent and running costs differ. The Slovenska location is larger and has seating, so prices there are slightly higher. The difference is fifty cents on main dishes.
faqN.skupina.pitanje: Can I order for a large group?
faqN.skupina.odgovor: You can, but call at least two hours ahead so we can prepare it without a wait. For more than ten portions we agree an exact pick-up time. The family menu is designed for four people.
faqN.cakanje.pitanje: How long do I wait for my food?
faqN.cakanje.odgovor: Kebab and falafel are ready in five minutes; pizzas need about fifteen. Late on Friday and Saturday evenings the wait can be longer, so calling ahead is a good idea.
faqN.prilagoditi.odgovor: Of course. You can leave ingredients out or add them, order the sauce on the side, and have a dish made more or less spicy. Tell us when ordering — it is harder to fix once prepared.
faqN.popusti.odgovor: The family menu is cheaper than ordering separately, and the student voucher is valid all day. We do not advertise occasional promotions on the website; we post them on social media.
faqN.reklamacija.pitanje: What if something is wrong with my order?
faqN.reklamacija.odgovor: Call the location where you ordered and we will tell you what happens next. If the mistake is ours, we replace the dish at no extra cost. For delivery orders, also contact Wolt or Glovo.
seoK.uvod: Halal döner kebab in central Ljubljana, with meat carved by hand from the vertical grill. We stay open longer than most — until five in the morning at Trubarjeva on weekends. We bake our bread daily, and the meat marinates for twenty-four hours to a family recipe dating from 1998.
seoK.b3t: Döner is a Turkish dish in which layers of marinated meat are stacked on a vertical spit and slowly cooked beside a heat source. The name means “turning” — the spit rotates constantly so the meat cooks evenly. Once the outer layer is done it is carved off and served, while the inside keeps cooking.
seoK.b4t: We stack the meat on the spit in the evening so the marinade works through overnight. In the morning the spit goes on the grill, where it cooks slowly all day. We carve by hand rather than by machine: the slices are thicker and stay juicy. The bread goes on the grill for a moment before filling, so it stays soft inside and crisp outside.
seoK.q1p: What meat is in the kebab?
seoK.q1o: A mix of beef and veal, both halal. Chicken döner is prepared on a separate spit so the meats do not mix.
seoK.q2p: What is the difference between kebab in bread and in yufka?
seoK.q2o: In bread the portion is larger and more filling; the yufka is thin and tightly wrapped, so it suits eating on the move. The filling is the same.
seoK.q3o: The standard one is not. The dürüm has a sharper dressing, and with any dish you can order the spicy sauce on the side or leave it out.
seoP.uvod: Pizzas from dough proofed for twenty-four hours, baked on a stone slab at high heat. All ingredients are halal, including the salami and ham — which means you can order a pizza here that is often unavailable elsewhere. The offering is the same at both locations.
seoP.b3t: Dough that proofs longer develops more flavour and is easier to digest, because the yeast consumes most of the sugars. Ours rests for twenty-four hours in the fridge, which slows the rise and gives the crust the bubbles that puff up in the oven. Fast dough cannot do that, however hot the oven.
seoP.b4t: We stretch the pizza by hand, never with a rolling pin, so the rim stays airy. It bakes on a stone slab, which draws out moisture and gives the base its crispness. Because the oven is hot, baking takes only a few minutes — which is why we make pizzas to order and not in advance.
seoP.q1o: Yes. All the meat toppings are halal, there is no pork in the kitchen at all, and the dough contains no alcohol.
seoP.q2o: Margherita and vegetariana are vegetarian. Every pizza on the menu is labelled if it is vegetarian.
seoP.q3p: How long do I wait for a pizza?
seoP.q3o: About fifteen minutes, because we only make it once you order. On weekend evenings it can take longer.
seoB.uvod: Halal burgers from freshly minced meat and buns we bake ourselves. We mince the meat every day and never freeze it — the patty hits the grill within a few hours of mincing. That is exactly why we do not prepare burgers in advance, and why at the busiest times you may wait a few minutes longer.
seoB.b3t: The ratio of lean meat to fat. Too little fat and the patty is dry; too much and it falls apart on the grill. We keep to roughly eighty percent lean, which is enough to stay juicy while holding together. We salt the meat only just before grilling, because salt draws out water if added earlier.
seoB.b4t: We press the patty onto a hot grill and turn it no more than once, so a proper crust forms. We halve the bun and lay it on the grill for half a minute, so it takes on some fat and does not go soggy. We assemble in order: sauce, salad, meat, cheese — that way the bottom half stays dry to the last bite.
seoB.q1o: Yes. The beef comes from the same halal suppliers as the kebab meat, and there is no bacon in the kitchen at all.
seoB.q2p: Can I get a burger without cheese?
seoB.q2o: Of course. You can leave ingredients out or add them — just say so when ordering.
seoB.q3p: Do you have a vegetarian burger?
seoB.q3o: Not for now, but we do have falafel in yufka and the falafel plate, both fully plant-based.
seoF.uvod: Falafel from chickpeas, fresh herbs and sesame — fully plant-based, with no meat and no eggs. We shape the balls as we go and fry them only once you order, because falafel that waits loses its crispness within minutes. We serve it in yufka or as a plate with hummus and salad.
seoF.b3t: Falafel is a Middle Eastern dish of ground chickpeas seasoned with garlic, parsley and cumin. The chickpeas are not boiled but soaked overnight and then ground raw — and that is exactly what gives falafel its characteristically light centre. Cooked chickpeas would give a smooth paste that disintegrates in the oil.
seoF.b4t: We soak the chickpeas in the evening and grind them with the herbs in the morning. The mixture rests for an hour so it binds, then we shape the balls and roll them in sesame. We fry in oil that we change daily and in which nothing meat-based is ever fried — that way the falafel remains suitable for vegans too.
seoF.q1o: It is. It contains no meat, eggs or milk, and we fry it in separate oil in which nothing meat-based is fried.
seoF.q2o: The balls themselves do not, but the yufka and the pita do. If you avoid gluten, order the falafel plate without pita.
seoF.q3o: A thick paste of ground sesame, thinned with water and lemon. It contains sesame, which matters if you have allergies.
seoH.uvod: At Šeherezada every dish on the menu is halal, not just the kebab. That includes the burgers, the pizzas, the ćevapi and every sauce. There is no pork in the kitchen and we use no alcohol — neither in the dough nor in the marinades. We verify our suppliers' certificate once a year, and it hangs by the till in every location.
seoH.b3n: Why the whole menu, not just the kebab
seoH.b3t: Because a guest looking for halal food does not want to wonder every time which dish is safe and which is not. If only part of the menu is halal, they have to ask each time — and risk an imprecise answer. When everything is halal the question disappears, and the guest can choose freely, like everyone else.
seoH.b4t: We buy from three suppliers with a valid certificate and never source meat anywhere else, even when we run short. There is no pork on the premises, so cross-contact is not possible. Ingredients that often hide alcohol — vinegar, vanilla flavouring, certain sauces — we buy in alcohol-free versions.
seoH.q1o: Our meat suppliers hold the certificate, issued by recognised certification bodies in Slovenia and Austria.
seoH.q2o: No. There are no alcoholic drinks on the menu and we use no alcohol in preparing any dish.
seoH.q3p: Is the offering the same at all locations?
seoH.q3o: The offering is the same; only prices and opening hours differ. Halal applies everywhere without exception.
seoN.uvod: The location at Trubarjeva cesta 31 is open until five in the morning on Fridays and Saturdays, and until two on weekdays. It is our only location that runs that late — the Slovenska location closes at midnight, so for a late-night meal come to Trubarjeva rather than stand at a locked door.
seoN.b3t: At night the full menu runs, not a shortened version. Kebab and falafel come fastest, because the meat and the balls are ready and waiting; pizzas need about fifteen minutes, because we bake them only once you order. Drinks and sides are available until closing.
seoN.b4t: After midnight two people stay in the shop, one at the grill and one at the till. Since the rush is biggest once the bars close, we recommend placing your order by phone before you set out. We take the last order ten minutes before closing.
seoN.q1p: Which location is open at night?
seoN.q1o: Only Trubarjeva. Slovenska closes at midnight, so late in the evening come to Trubarjeva cesta 31.
seoN.q2o: Delivery depends on Wolt and Glovo, which often do not run at night. Pick-up at our counter works until closing.
seoN.q3o: We take the last order ten minutes before closing — so until 04:50 on Fridays and Saturdays.
seoD.uvod: We deliver through Wolt and Glovo, which cover central Ljubljana and the surrounding area. Delivery usually takes between twenty and forty-five minutes, depending on the hour and the weather. If you are in a hurry, order by phone and collect at the counter — that is when the food is freshest.
seoD.b3n: What travels well and what does not
seoD.b3t: Kebab and ćevapi survive the journey without trouble, because the bread shields them from cooling. Fries and falafel lose their crispness within fifteen minutes, so we pack them in perforated boxes to let the steam escape. We send pizzas uncut — if we slice them, the middle goes soft before it reaches your door.
seoD.b4t: We pack each dish separately and the sauces apart, so the bread does not go soggy. Hot and cold dishes never share a bag. If you order several dishes we stack them with the heavier ones at the bottom — the couriers ride bicycles, and otherwise the packaging shifts.
seoD.q1o: The area is set by Wolt and Glovo; they usually cover central Ljubljana and neighbourhoods up to about four kilometres out.
seoD.q2o: The price is set by the delivery services and varies with distance and time of day. It is shown in their app before you pay.
seoD.q3p: What if the order arrives cold?
seoD.q3o: Call the location and let us know. If the fault is ours we replace the dish; for the transport time, contact the delivery service as well.
seoS.uvod: We accept the student meal voucher at both open locations, throughout opening hours. The student menu includes a main course of your choice, soup, salad, an apple and a drink — a full meal, not just the main course. Any surcharge depends on the main course chosen and is always stated on the menu.
seoS.b3t: Under the rules of the subsidised student meal scheme, a meal must contain a main course, a side, fruit and a drink. For us that means a dish of your choice from the menu, soup or salad, an apple and a drink. The fruit and soup cannot be swapped for a second main course, because the rules do not allow it.
seoS.b4t: When ordering you show the voucher, choose a main course and say whether you want soup or salad. You settle the surcharge by card or cash. The voucher is valid once a day and cannot be used for the family menu or for dishes ordered through delivery.
seoS.q1p: Is the voucher valid all day?
seoS.q1o: It is valid throughout our opening hours, including late in the evening, but only once a day per person.
seoS.q2p: Which main courses can I choose?
seoS.q2o: Anything on the menu except the family menu. For pricier dishes the surcharge is higher, which is stated next to the price.
seoS.q3p: Can I use the voucher for delivery?
seoS.q3o: No. The subsidy applies only to collection in person at the location; those are the rules of the scheme.
seoDo.uvod: If you are looking for real döner in Ljubljana, we carve ours off the vertical spit to order, every time. The meat is strictly halal, seasoned to a recipe we have not changed since 2009. Have it in bread, in yufka or on a plate. At weekends our Trubarjeva location stays open until five in the morning, when most kitchens in town have long closed.
seoDo.b3n: What döner is and how it differs from kebab
seoDo.b3t: Döner is a Turkish preparation in which layers of meat are stacked on a vertical spit and roasted slowly beside a grill. The outer layer is carved off just before serving, which is why it is crisp outside and juicy inside at the same time. Kebab is the broader term and also covers meat from a horizontal spit or a grill. We serve both, but döner is what guests come looking for most often.
seoDo.b4t: We load the spit fresh every morning, never from frozen blocks. The meat is beef and veal with halal certification, from a supplier we have worked with for years. Vegetables are cut through the day and the sauces are our own. Because the spit roasts continuously, the meat at two in the morning is as fresh as at midday — which is exactly what guests ask us most at night.
seoDo.q1p: What meat is your döner made from?
seoDo.q1o: Beef and veal, both halal certified. There is no pork in our kitchen and there never has been. Chicken döner is available as a separate dish.
seoDo.q2p: What is the difference between döner in bread and in yufka?
seoDo.q2o: In bread you get a thicker flatbread that fills you up more; yufka is thin dough wrapped around the filling, so the dish feels lighter. The amount of meat is the same — only the dough differs.
seoDo.q3p: How late can I order döner?
seoDo.q3o: At Trubarjeva until five in the morning on Fridays and Saturdays, and until two on weekdays. At Slovenska until midnight. We take the last order about fifteen minutes before closing.
kontakt.uvod: Both locations are in central Ljubljana, a few minutes' walk apart. Below are the exact addresses, phone numbers and opening hours — if you are in a hurry, just call; we pick up in the middle of the night too.
kontakt.potT: Trubarjeva cesta is a pedestrian street just off Prešeren Square — from there it is about a five-minute walk along the water. The Slovenska cesta location sits on the city's main axis, opposite a bus stop. Coming by train, both are roughly fifteen minutes on foot from the railway station.
kontakt.parkingT: There is no street parking in the inner centre. The nearest garages are by Kongresni trg and behind the market; both are open at night as well. On weekend evenings it is easiest to park a little further out and walk in, as traffic through the centre is restricted.
kontakt.placiloT: We take cash and cards. You can order by phone and pick up at the counter, use Wolt or Glovo for delivery, or simply walk in — most dishes are ready within a few minutes.
blog.uvod: Short guides to what people look for most in Ljubljana: what each dish actually is, how we make it, and where you can get it at which hour. No embellishment — if we do not do something, it says so.
